title: Chapter 33: A Glimpse of Light and the Shadow of Foreboding
content:
Chapter 33:

A Glimpse of Light and the Shadow of Foreboding

The somewhat pre-established harmonious negotiation with Beatrice concluded, and Subaru successfully secured her cooperation.

It was a result where he couldn’t deny the feeling of having heavily clung to her compassion, but lamenting his lack of power regarding that matter would all be put off until later.

Achieving the objective came first, reflection could come later. Because if he started saying things while in the middle of a “what if,” there would be no end to it.

Suddenly wondering about the time, Subaru touched his own chin.

The interior of the Forbidden Library was completely isolated from the outside world, and there was absolutely no means to know the outside time from within. Not even a crystal stone was placed in a clock’s stead, and looking at the young girl who was the librarian, he thought she lived a rather free lifestyle in that sense.

From the feel of the stubble on his chin, it had been around seventeen hours since he shaved. It was probably around 10:00 PM.

Considering he started his deep sleep on Emilia’s lap just after noon, that was an outrageous level of oversleeping.

Having enthusiastically declared he couldn’t waste even a single second, only for that to happen, he felt more and more hopeless the more he thought back on it.

Since there would be no end to it if he started self-loathing, Subaru cut to the main topic with Beatrice, whose dissatisfaction gauge seemed completely full.

To what extent could he explain things to her without touching on its core?

Without neglecting his caution towards the black haze, intending to resolve each of his doubts one by one,

“…Do you want to know about curse arts users in detail?”

“Yeah. Unlike magicians or spirit users, I know there are users of that kind of branch, but I don’t have any knowledge beyond that.”

“You’re a guy who wants to ask about strange things again, in fact. Even if you know about those kinds of people, there’s not a shred of benefit, I suppose.”

Just like when she only mentioned it briefly before, Beatrice’s expression when speaking of curses was not bright. She had decisively stated that she didn’t like their approach to mana, but this time it was necessary to cut even deeper into it.

“I think basically, it’s a branch that can only be used to cause trouble for others, right? I heard it was popular in the countries to the north or something.”

“If you know that much, it feels unnecessary to say, I suppose. —Making the target contract an illness through a curse, or imposing a restriction forbidding certain actions, or purely reaping their life… It’s a branch with a bad personality, in fact.”

“Well, it’s true they say tools depend on how they’re used, but if it’s that biased, I can’t see any use for it other than dragging others down.”

That was exactly why they were curse arts. A ‘curse,’ so to speak.

A supernatural power to degrade others was, after all, an evil that could likely arise in any culture or society. Though he thought it was only in this world that it possessed enough efficacy to actually affect others.

Ushi-no-toki Mairi, depending on how you looked at it, was also in the realm of curses.

While thinking such things, Subaru leaned forward to make the tight-lipped Beatrice speak,

“So then, I want to ask… how can you prevent a curse?”

Intercepting the curse arts user; this in itself was difficult unless you could grasp the opponent’s true identity. But the advantage Subaru held in this situation boiled down to a single point: he knew an attack was coming.

Even if he didn’t know the true identity of the curse arts user, since he knew the curse arts user would use ‘curses,’ taking measures to prevent them was an obvious but reasonable strategy. A brilliant idea, if he did say so himself.

However,

“You can’t, in fact.”

“—Huh?”

“There is no method to prevent a curse once it has activated, in fact. A curse will not disappear until it exerts its efficacy and fulfills the curse upon the target, I suppose.”

“Instant Death Resistance Nullification, seriously…”

At Beatrice’s indifferently stated words, Subaru’s heart almost broke prematurely.

A surprise attack with an Instant Death Resistance Nullification spell—just thinking about it, it was a combat condition that would invite a mountain of bashing.

“To top it off, an incantation the moment combat starts. We have no way to resist… hey, this is checkmate. It’s a checkmate. This is the very definition of a shit game!”

Scratching his head, he reconfirmed the bad situation he was placed in.

The faint bright conditions that had surfaced just moments ago were smashed to pieces, and Subaru’s brain boiled as it searched for another strategy.

Baron Ashura state, half his face blue with despair, the other half red with unyielding spirit. To such a Subaru, Beatrice,

“However, that’s strictly speaking about an activated curse, in fact.”

Said that, loosening her lips as if revealing the trick.

Breathing out a “Huh?”, Subaru raised his face and Beatrice’s smug face was reflected in his eyes. The girl’s expression said, ‘You fell for it hook, line, and sinker,’ but his chest was completely frozen.

At the tremendous temperature difference that occurred upon reaching this point, she rolled her eyes just a little and,

“…There isn’t really any need to get that angry, in fact.”

“I, Seriously, Might, Cry.”

Killing as much emotion as possible in broken speech, he finally replied.

Inside, his chest was seething with abuse and insults directed at Beatrice, but he wanted to avoid letting that out and arguing with her right now.

After all, it finally seemed like a glimmer of optimism was starting to appear.

Raising a finger as if to collect herself, Beatrice lectured,

“As said earlier, there is no means to prevent a curse once it has activated, I suppose. However, if it’s a curse before activation, it can be interfered with, in fact. Before activation, it’s not a curse but merely a spell rite, so dispelling it can be easily done by an existence with a certain degree of ability, I suppose.”

“For example?”

“In this mansion, first Betty. Bubby of course. Also Roswaal… it might be impossible for the three little girls, in fact. Ah, it’s impossible for you too, in fact.”

“I know that firsthand…”

—I was well taken care of the first and second times.

Setting that aside, Subaru pressed Beatrice,

“How do you make out a spell rite before activation? I mean, does a curse require preparation before being activated?”

“Of course it does, in fact. If you handle a spell rite with strong efficacy, the burden becomes just as heavy on the caster’s end. The same holds true for everything, I suppose. That aspect is especially strong with curses, in fact. Considering their anti-personnel effect, you could say it’s a natural price to pay, I suppose.”

“Umm, does that price for a curse… is there any way to guess what it is?”

Feeling like grasping at straws, at that question Beatrice closed one eye, pondered for a moment, then licked her lips and,

“The details change depending on what effect the curse being performed has, in fact. But, there is an absolutely inescapable rule, I suppose.”

“Inescapable, rule…”

Swallowing his breath, he urged Beatrice to continue where she cut off her words.

At the plea in Subaru’s gaze, Beatrice lightly pulled back her chin and,

“—Contact with the target the curse is being performed on. This is an essential condition, in fact.”

Told him that.

The moment that information entered his head, Subaru’s brain spun dizzily. To perform a curse, contact between the user and the target is necessary. This meant that both the first and second times, Subaru himself had confronted that curse arts user. —Searching his memory, trying to recall that person.

“Excluding the members of the mansion…”

Omitting their existences as potential targets of the curse, Subaru recalled his days during the first eight days.

Living as a servant in the mansion, a time when he supposedly had almost no opportunities to interact with anyone other than the people related to the mansion. During that time, if there was an outside existence Subaru could have possibly come into contact with—

“—The village at the foot of the mountain.”

Both the first and second times, Subaru had visited that village.

And thinking back, both times he went to the village were during the day of the crucial fourth day. The pattern crossed his mind: having a curse spell cast on him by the curse arts user in the village, returning to the mansion right after, the activation of the curse—leading to death.

If the curse arts user was staying in the village, the case where Rem became the target of the curse in the fourth loop also made sense.

It was simply a matter of her going to the village during that loop and being chosen as the curse arts user’s target. Depending on the circumstances, it might have been Ram, and if he had carelessly visited the village, it would likely have been Subaru after all.

It connects. It connects. Everything connected.

“Beako. Do you know roughly how many residents live in the village closest to this mansion?”

Suddenly presented with a topic of different content, Beatrice furrowed her brows in incomprehension. But it was probably because Subaru’s expression was so serious. Without pointing it out, she shook her head side to side,

“No idea, in fact. Sorry, but excluding this Forbidden Library, Betty doesn’t even possess much knowledge about the inside of the mansion, I suppose.”

“I see. No, it’s fine. That was aiming a little high. Besides, I can just ask Roswaal about that much… Now what’s left is,”

Was the curse arts user among the residents, or were they a sojourner?

In the latter case, tracking them down wouldn’t be that difficult. He could purely ask the people of the village about it and smoke out the user. Conversely, in the former case, deducing it would become an extremely difficult task. If they had prepared that thoroughly, he’d throw his hands up, but—

“But that possibility is actually slim.”

If he concluded that this incident was tied to the Royal Selection, the severing of the Royal Family due to an epidemic was an event from only about half a year ago.

Including the time it took for Emilia’s name to be raised as a royal candidate and for the framework of the Royal Selection to be created, the current situation should be a fresh battlefield that had only just been formed within the past three or four months.

He couldn’t imagine there being someone with the foresight to take measures such as hiding a curse arts user among the villagers in advance. If such a person existed, he could only think they were a clairvoyant or someone who “had known of the Royal Selection’s occurrence beforehand.”

If he thought about it like that,

“The curse arts user is an outsider. And finding them isn’t exactly a high-difficulty case…!”

Saying it aloud, Subaru began to search for holes in his own thinking.

Although there were a few points to correct, the deduction as a main outline wasn’t bad. To begin with, from the curse art user’s perspective, this was a situation before taking action. Unless they were a god or a demon, they couldn’t know that their existence had been exposed at this point.

Looking up, his gaze wandered trying to look at a clock, but there was none.

Clicking his tongue, yet recalling his measurement of the stubble timer from earlier, he chewed over the fact that it was still ‘the night of the second day.’

Against the fourth day, when the situation would begin its tilt towards the worst, he still had a one-day grace period.

That meant, in other words, it made a surprise attack on the curse arts user from his side possible.

“I grabbed your tail, damn it…! I didn’t get killed once and almost killed a second time for nothing, you piece of shit!”

He saw the light. The situation changed.

The despair opened up, and he felt as if hope was shining in from the other side; Subaru involuntarily clenched his fists and trembled his voice in delight.

Against him rejoicing at the favorable turn of events like that, Beatrice, who had been left behind partway through, looked dissatisfied.

She flushed her adorable cheeks, pouted her lips to express her displeasure, and,

“Asking someone for cooperation, and then taking that attitude, what is that about, I suppose. If my words just now were helpful, isn’t there something you should say to Betty, in fact.”

“Oh, yeah! You saved me, thanks to you I saw the light! I super love you Beako!”

“Wha—?!”

Jumping at her, slipping his hands under her armpits and lifting her light body, Subaru hoisted Beatrice above his head and spun around and around.

Despite wearing a luxurious dress, the young girl’s body was light as a feather. Since Subaru’s mood was also soaring, due to the synergistic effect, the speed of the spin doubled, and then doubled again.

“Let g… put me down, I suppose!”

“Hahaha, right now I feel like I could even fly in the sky. No, should we just fly together, Beako?! I can fly! You can fly!”

“Don’t get carried away, in fact—!”

“Jamupuroh?!”

Magical power was blasted at close range from directly above, and taking a direct hit, he was slammed into the ground in an incomprehensible posture.

The impact that entered from his head traveled through his body and exited straight through his rear. Landing on his butt, his eyes spun at the torrent of mana raging inside his body.

Meanwhile, Beatrice, who had done it, was freed from Subaru’s grip and flew in a magnificent parabola with her small stature.

However, the body of the young girl, which seemed like it would crash into somewhere, suddenly came to a sudden stop in midair. Flipping her body softly, her skirt hem fluttering, she landed lightly on the floor of the library with elegant quietness.

She looked down at Subaru, who was still unseemly shaking his head on the ground, and snorted with a familiar attitude,

“Getting carried away and acting familiar like that is why you have a painful experience, I suppose.”

“That’s not the only thing I experienced though. —They were white.”

“—?! Eat this, I suppose!”

“Dorowazu?!”

A second shot struck straight through Subaru’s jaw, lightly blowing his body deep into the library. Rolling over and over, he crashed into the stepladder and ended up crushed beneath the falling wood. With various jagged corners hitting him, his eyes tearing up from the extraordinary pain,

“I maxed out my affection gauge and let loose a super special, and this is what I get?! Tell me, what were you dissatisfied with!”

“Hugging me, lifting me like a child, swinging me around, looking at my underwear, and spouting superficial words of love, all of it, in fact! Betty’s already angry at your very existence, I suppose!”

“Complete denial of my existence is sad so stop it! It reminds me of my shut-in days, even though it wasn’t that long ago.”

Thinking back, his shut-in days felt like they were far in the past.

Actually, in terms of distance, he felt like he had come so far it could no longer be calculated; 

I wonder if everyone is doing well.

At any rate,

“Going full circle and calming down, the situation has gotten quite a bit better. …Tonight is tough, but around tomorrow I’ll go to the village and…”

Search for the curse arts user’s true identity, he thought.

Since he probably couldn’t go alone, he would likely have to accompany either Ram or Rem. And if he considered a confrontation with the curse art user on the spot, having the two who excelled in combat power accompany him seemed like an essential condition.

If things went well, they would defeat the curse arts user, and if things went even better, if it became clear that the relationship between Subaru and the curse arts user was a clean slate, the situation would be a grand finale.

Mission 2 ‘Conquer Roswaal Manor’ clear.

“Compared to Mission 1, the difficulty level was super high, seriously.”

If he recalled correctly, Mission 1 was ‘Defeat the Thugs,’ so looking back, he really had come a long way.

He thought back on the offense and defense with the thugs, which felt like a long time ago before he knew it, and then reflected anew on his days in the mansion.

He knew he was getting ahead of himself, but the dead end where he couldn’t do anything was finally about to open up. He wanted them to forgive this level of high spirits.

Was there anything else he needed to resolve, Subaru did not neglect to check his footing.

It was precisely because the situation was beginning to take a favorable turn that he suspected there might be a pitfall there. It was a sense of caution born from cowardice, but there was a word that suddenly caught in that net of caution. It was, yes,

“The Witch’s, lingering scent…”

“What is it, in fact.”

“Right. The Witch. Rem too…”

Uttering that single word, numerous scenes revived in his memory.

The word ‘Witch’ that appeared frequently everywhere; Subaru had not yet gained the true meaning of that word as knowledge.

The Witch of this world that Subaru knew was merely a fragment of an extremely short episode called ‘The Witch of Envy’ that was published as a fairy tale.

However, thinking back, even during the loops on his first day summoned. And even within the repetitions in the mansion this time, that name had shown its face several times.

Subaru raised his face and looked at Beatrice, who furrowed her brows suspiciously.

He had a slight anxiety about whether she would answer. After all, the previous time he had spoken of this, he was flatly cut off by Ram, and as for Rem, it had even become her motive to attack him.

Even Emilia seemed to harbor some strong resistance to it. Therefore, carrying that anxiety,

“Beako. —Do you know about the Witch?”

“————”

To his question, however, an immediate reply did not return.

Beatrice closed her eyes at the word that vibrated her eardrums, and fell silent as if to verify those words.

Subaru, too, merely waited, his heart stirred by her reaction.

Thinking, surely that single phrase just now hadn’t touched her heartstrings again.

“The one who drinks the world dry. The Queen of the Castle of Shadows. —The Witch of Envy.”

At the suddenly muttered words, Subaru swallowed his breath and his eyes widened.

Not bringing Subaru’s reaction into her sight, Beatrice let out a melancholic sigh from her lips and,

“In this world, the word Witch points to only one single existence, in fact. And, it’s an existence that is considered taboo to even speak of, I suppose.”

“Everyone fears her, everyone dreads her, and no one can defy her.”

“Yes, that’s it, in fact. Rather, your question asking if Betty knows of her is questionable, in fact. There’s no way you shouldn’t know, I suppose. In this world, the Witch’s name is taught right after one’s parents’ names and family’s names, in fact.”

“That’s, an exaggeration…”

Trying to laugh it off, he swallowed his words, unable to find a shred of a joke in Beatrice’s expression.

If what she just said wasn’t a joke, it was undoubtedly an abominable symbol to the world, and—.

“The Witch of Envy Satella. —The worst calamity, who devoured all six Witches who bore the names of the great sins that once existed, and destroyed half the world, in fact.”

Stating it in a voice frozen of emotion, Beatrice kept her eyes closed.

At that name he remembered hearing, Subaru let out a short breath of “Hah,” and the weight of the name thrown at him sealed even his ability to flinch.

“They say she ruled the night. They say she couldn’t understand human words. They say she envied everything in this world. They say no one who saw her face survived. They say her body will never rot, never wither, and never perish. They say that even though she was sealed with the power of the Dragon, the Hero, and the Sage, they were unable to destroy her body.”

Stating it fluidly, Beatrice did not allow Subaru to interject words.

Then, as if to conclude the listed information, she placed a final preface of “They say,” and said.

“—Her body was that of a silver-haired half-elf.”
